cards.b: Random access memory: volatile primary memory that holds programs and data currently in use. Read and write.
Read-only memory: non-volatile primary memory that stores the bootstrap (start-up instructions that load the OS).
Memory that loses its contents when the power is turned off.
RAM is volatile. Secondary storage is non-volatile so data and programs are kept when the power is off.
When RAM is full, part of secondary storage is used as extra memory. Pages are swapped in and out, which is slower than RAM.
Tiny areas of a spinning platter are magnetised one way or the other. A read/write head reads or changes them. Example: hard disk drive.
A laser reads pits and lands on a spinning disc, which reflect light differently. Examples: CD, DVD, Blu-ray.
Flash memory with no moving parts; transistors trap or release charge for 1 and 0. Examples: SSD, USB stick, SD card.
SSD: faster, silent, durable, low power, but costs more per GB. HDD: cheaper per GB, larger capacity, but has moving parts.
Data stored on remote servers accessed over the internet. Needs a connection; the provider holds your data.
Access from any device anywhere, easy sharing, automatic backup, and capacity easily increased.
Network interface card: hardware that connects a device to a network, wired or wireless. It holds the MAC address.
Unique 48-bit address set by the manufacturer, shown as six pairs of hex digits. First half identifies the manufacturer.
IPv4: 32 bits, four numbers 0–255. IPv6: 128 bits, eight groups of hex digits. IPv6 exists because IPv4 addresses are running out.
Connects different networks, reads the destination IP address of packets and sends them on the best route. Often assigns IP addresses.

short.q: Describe how data is stored and read on a magnetic hard disk drive.
short.model: The platter surface is split into tiny areas that are magnetised one way or the other to represent 1 and 0. As the platters spin, a read/write head over the surface reads or changes the magnetisation.

short.q: Explain why a computer becomes slower when it relies heavily on virtual memory.
short.model: Data must be swapped between RAM and secondary storage, which is much slower to access than RAM, so the CPU waits for data.
points: data swapped between RAM and secondary storage
secondary storage is slower than RAM

short.q: A student chooses an SSD instead of an HDD for a laptop. Give two reasons.
short.model: An SSD has no moving parts so is more durable if the laptop is knocked, and it is faster to read and write, silent and uses less power.

short.q: Give two benefits and one drawback of storing photos in cloud storage.
short.model: Benefits: photos are accessible from any device with internet and are backed up if the phone is lost. Drawback: an internet connection is needed (and the data is held by a third party).

short.q: Describe the role of a router in a home network.
short.model: It connects the home network to the internet. It reads the destination IP address of each packet and sends it on the best route, and usually assigns IP addresses to devices.
points: uses destination IP address to send packets
assigns IP addresses / provides Wi-Fi or firewall
